messages:
alex: anyone else seeing a big spike in gpu pod preempts in eu-west1? ~50 evictions in the last hour, apps report increased latency :grimacing:
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-042 (gpu-evict-eu-west1) - paging oncall
mira: yup, noticed it around 06:12UTC. pattern is weird: lots of small batch jobs with a reserved annotation are blocking binpack defrag, scheduler is splitting gangs and then preempting lower-priority replica pods
jorge: checked scheduler logs, snippet:
```
I0406 06:11:23 scheduler.go:412] Pod default/train-xyz failed Fit at node gpu-node-32: PodFitsResources: Insufficient contiguous gpus
I0406 06:11:24 scheduler.go:420] Preempting pod default/worker-4 on gpu-node-12 to satisfy train-xyz (priority 100 > 50)
```
cleo: that "Insufficient contiguous gpus" message is the key. our topology policy wants rack-local contiguous GPUs for inference pods (softAffinity: required) — but we have many thin-pool reservations from nightly batch jobs with `reserved: true` which fragment nodes
alex: so two simultaneous things: (1) thin reservations hold 1-2 gpus across many nodes (low util), (2) placement policy prefers contiguous within a rack -> scheduler struggles to pack, ends up preempting many small replicas to satisfy contiguous requirement
mira: exact. the defrag controller can't run because the descheduler cron is disabled during business hours (we flipped it last month during a bad rollout)
jorge: quick numbers: ~120 GPUs total in eu-west1 pool, fragmentation means ~18% unusable for contiguous requests. evictions jumped when two heavy inference rollouts started at 06:10UTC
cleo: mitigation options:
- relax topology requirement from `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` -> `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`
- enable descheduler runs (evict low-priority low-util pods) during off-peak + dry-run first
- temporary burst capacity (add 8 gpus) while we defrag
- patch batch jobs to use `preemptionPolicy: Never` + `priorityClass: low` so they get descheduled first
alex: cost question — if we add burst 8 gpus as spot, estimate ~€7k/month. if we change scheduling rules, risk of slightly more cross-rack bandwidth and perf variance for some latency-sensitive workloads
mira: preference: avoid costs first, try policy change + single canary rollout. we should also tweak the scheduler predicate to allow non-contiguous placement for non-latency-critical models
jorge: quick canary plan:
- Mira to patch staging scheduler config to preferInsteadOfRequire at 07:30UTC (canary on 10% traffic)
- Run descheduler dry-run at 08:00UTC to validate eviction candidates
- If dry-run looks sane, enable descheduler at 02:00UTC tomorrow for full defrag
cleo: will open a change request: CR-4482 to update `reserved` job annotation semantics and add a `defer-window` so long-lived reservations don't fragment during peak
ops-bot: note: paging silence requested by @mira for 2 hours to avoid noise while we run the canary :white_check_mark:
alex: small fix we can attempt now: add a temporary scheduler plugin config to allow splitting a gang across racks for pods with label `app: background-train` (non-critical) — low-risk, immediate
mira: ok I'll push the staging patch and post results here. if evictions continue after policy change, we flip the burst capacity plan and schedule the descheduler earlier
jorge: logging/metrics TODOs: add a dashboard for "contiguous-gpu-availability" (gpus usable for k contiguous=1..8) and a per-topology fragmentation heatmap to inform autoscaler decisions
cleo: i'm adding cost impact rows to CR-4482 (spot vs reserved vs no-change) — will ping finance if we need burst capacity
alex: thanks team. action items summarized:
- mira: push scheduler config patch to staging (07:30UTC) and report
- mir a: run descheduler dry-run (08:00UTC)
- cleo: CR-4482 open + update reserved semantics
- jorge: dashboard for contiguous-gpu-availability
- alex: temporary scheduler plugin for non-critical app label

mira: sending a quick note to the infra-oncall channel once staging patch is up. will paste the staging logs here. :rocket:
